facts.statement: The species Linhevenator tani was named and described in 2011 by Xu Xing, Tan Qingwei, Corwin Sullivan, Han Fenglu, and Xiao Dong.
facts.quote: The type species Linhevenator tani was named and described in 2011 by Xu Xing, Tan Qingwei, Corwin Sullivan, Han Fenglu and Xiao Dong.

facts.statement: Linhevenator possessed a second toe similar to dromaeosaurids that carried a sickle-claw larger than those found in basal troodontids.
facts.quote: Linhevenator has a dromaeosaurid-like pedal digit II, carrying a sickle-claw larger than that of basal troodontids.

facts.statement: Linhevenator lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Linhevenator is a genus of short-armed troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) Bayan Mandahu Formation of Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia, China.

facts.statement: Linhevenator tani lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago during the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Linhevenator tani es la única especie conocida del género extinto Linhevenator es un género de dinosaurio terópodo troodóntido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Linhevenator is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Linhevenator was classified as a derived troodontid in a phylogenetic analysis, appearing in a polytomy with Troodon and a clade containing Zanabazar and Saurornithoides.
facts.quote: Linhevenator was assigned to the Troodontidae by the describers. It possesses a combination of "primitive" (basal) and derived characters, but was found to be a derived troodontid in a phylogenetic analysis, in a polytomy with Troodon and a clade formed by Zanabazar and Saurornithoides.

facts.statement: Researchers view Linhevenator's position as evidence of an evolutionary trend in Troodontidae involving the shortening of forelimbs and parallel evolution of large foot claws in both troodontids and dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Esta posición es vista por los autores como una indicación de una tendencia evolutiva en la familia Troodontidae de un acortamiento de los miembros delanteros y de una evolución paralela de grandes garras en los pies tanto en los troodóntidos como en los dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: As troodontids, Linhevenator possessed sickle-claws, raptorial hands, and high encephalization quotients indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
facts.quote: Troodontids have sickle-claws and raptorial hands, and some of the highest non-avian encephalization quotients, meaning they were behaviourally advanced and had keen senses.

facts.statement: The first toe of Linhevenator was preserved in a lateral position rather than pointing forward.
facts.quote: El primer dedo del pie estaba preservado en una posición lateral, en vez de apuntar hacia adelante.

facts.statement: The generic name Linhevenator combines a reference to the Linhe region with the Latin word for hunter, while the species name honors Professor Tan Lin.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico combina una referencia a la región de Linhe con el término latino venator, que traduce "cazador". El nombre de la especie honra al profesor Tan Lin.
